analysis:
The PR changes only CI lane size requests in .github/workflows/provider-plan.yml (head lines 149-166 comments, 184-195 lane table), a changelog entry, and docs/developer/build.md (interim size table and explanatory text). Test lanes move from unsigned 4x16/4x24 to the signed 8x16, and GPU shard 2 moves to 12x32. Build lanes are unchanged. The edits are CI resource-shape parameters passed to darkbloom-route.yml, which was not supplied. No workflow permissions, triggers, secrets, checkout configuration, action pins, or tree-lookup and skip logic changed. The `permissions: {}` setting on the route job and the `contents: read` setting on the other jobs are unchanged. No provider runtime code was touched, so the canonical provider threat model entries are not affected: T-041 (prefix cache), TB-002, TB-003, A-015 through A-017, and the attestation boundaries.

The only residual concern is availability and reliability of CI. Runtime shard 2, Provider Unit Tests shard 2, and GPU shards 1 and 3 run with less than the 1.25 memory margin on 16 GiB, so they may be flaky. This is a test-quality matter, not a security regression. The docs state it openly. The docs say scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py must be kept in sync with the lane table, but that file was not supplied, so I could not check that it is consistent. This does not affect any security conclusion. No findings.
